Beginner.learningGoal: Write generic functions and types with simple constraints.
gotchas: T needs Equatable or Comparable before == or < compile
Generic type parameters are inferred, so a literal can pick an unexpected type
Generic functions are not the same as Any
goodSolutionShows: One generic function replacing several overloads
A small generic container (Stack or Queue) with value semantics
shapeHints: a generic Stack with push, pop and peek
a function that finds the maximum of any Comparable sequence
a generic Pair swap and map

Intermediate.learningGoal: Use protocols with associated types and generic constraints between them.
gotchas: Associated types must be pinned (where Item == Int) before they can be compared
A protocol with an associated type cannot be a plain existential without any
Type inference can fail where two sequences share an element type only by constraint
goodSolutionShows: Constraints with where Element == and associated type equality
A generic function over two Sequence types
Type-erased wrapper only if truly needed
shapeHints: a Repository protocol with an Entity associated type
merging two sequences of the same element type
a generic Cache keyed by Hashable

Advanced.learningGoal: Build generic abstractions with primary associated types, conditional conformances and overload resolution.
gotchas: Specialisation vs dynamic dispatch of generic requirement implementations
Overloads that differ only by constraint and the most specific one chosen
Associated type defaulting and inference from implementations
goodSolutionShows: A protocol with primary associated types used as some Collection<Int> or any Collection<Int>
Minimal API surface with documented constraints
shapeHints: a generic Pipeline with chained stages
a Result-like Either type with Functor operations

Expert.learningGoal: Design generic abstractions where dispatch, specialisation and conditional conformance interact, and prove which implementation runs.
gotchas: A requirement implemented in a protocol extension is dispatched dynamically while a non-requirement is dispatched statically from a generic context, so the same call can run different code inside and outside a generic function
Overloads constrained differently are chosen at compile time, so a generic caller only sees the constraints it declared
Conditional conformances stack, so Array<Array<Int>> conforms only if the inner conformance holds and the observable result depends on which layer supplies it
goodSolutionShows: Tests that call one operation through a concrete type and through a generic function and assert which implementation ran
Minimal constraints declared once, with primary associated types on the protocol for the public API
Conditional conformance with a documented, tested fallback path
shapeHints: a Describable protocol with a default and specialised implementations for collections
a Pipeline<Input, Output> composing stages with different constraints
a Mergeable protocol with Array and Dictionary conformances and a generic merge-all
